q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Investment Fund from the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund of the Government of India?

options.A: Both the funds are fed by the cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel
options.B: The National Investment Fund is credited mainly with the proceeds of disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises, whereas the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is financed mainly by a cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel
options.C: The National Investment Fund is financed by a cess on petrol and diesel, whereas the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is credited with the proceeds of disinvestment
options.D: The National Investment Fund holds the collections under the small savings schemes, whereas the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund holds the balances of the provident funds

e: The National Investment Fund is credited mainly with disinvestment proceeds of Central Public Sector Enterprises. The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is financed mainly by a cess on petrol and high speed diesel.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Revenue Section from the Capital Section of the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Both the sections deal only with the receipts and expenditure on revenue account
options.B: The Revenue Section is a part of the Public Account of India, whereas the Capital Section is a part of the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: The Revenue Section deals with the revenue receipts of the Government and the expenditure met from them on revenue account, whereas the Capital Section deals with the capital receipts, including the public debt and the recoveries of loans, and the capital disbursements of the Government
options.D: The Revenue Section deals with the public debt of the Government, whereas the Capital Section deals with the tax receipts of the Government

e: The Revenue Section of the Consolidated Fund deals with revenue receipts and expenditure met from them on revenue account. The Capital Section deals with capital receipts, including public debt and loan recoveries, and capital disbursements.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the treatment of the preliminary expenses of surveys and investigations in the two situations?

options.A: Where the project surveyed is subsequently sanctioned and taken up for construction, the preliminary expenses form part of the capital cost of the work, whereas where the project is ultimately abandoned and not taken up, the preliminary expenses are charged to revenue as ordinary working expenses
options.B: In both the situations, the preliminary expenses are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Where the project is taken up, the preliminary expenses are charged to revenue, whereas where it is abandoned, they are added to the capital cost of the work
options.D: In both the situations, the preliminary expenses are kept permanently under a suspense head

e: Preliminary survey expenses form part of the capital cost when the project is later sanctioned and taken up. If the project is abandoned, the expenses cannot be capitalised and are charged to revenue as ordinary working expenses.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'appropriation audit' from 'propriety audit' conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

options.A: Both the audits are concerned only with the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.B: Appropriation audit examines expenditure against the canons of financial propriety, whereas propriety audit verifies the availability of grants
options.C: Appropriation audit is conducted by the Accounts Department as an internal check, whereas propriety audit is conducted by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Appropriation audit verifies that the moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made by Parliament, whereas propriety audit examines expenditure against the canons of financial propriety, bringing out cases of wasteful, infructuous or avoidable expenditure

e: Appropriation audit verifies that disbursed moneys were legally available for and applied to the services Parliament granted them for. Propriety audit tests expenditure against canons of financial propriety, bringing out wasteful or avoidable spending.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Zero-Based Budgeting from performance budgeting?

options.A: Both the systems build the estimates of a year by adding a percentage increase to the expenditure of the previous year
options.B: Under Zero-Based Budgeting, every programme and item of expenditure is justified afresh from a zero base, without assuming that the existing level of expenditure will continue, whereas performance budgeting presents the estimates in terms of functions, programmes and activities, relating the financial outlays to the physical targets and results expected
options.C: Zero-Based Budgeting relates outlays to physical targets, whereas performance budgeting justifies every item afresh from a zero base
options.D: Zero-Based Budgeting is used only for the Capital Budget, whereas performance budgeting is used only for the Earnings Budget

e: Under Zero-Based Budgeting every programme is justified afresh from a zero base with no assumed continuation. Performance budgeting presents estimates by functions, programmes and activities, relating outlays to physical targets and results.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the monthly financial review of a zonal railway from its Appropriation Accounts?

options.A: Both the documents are prepared after the close of the year for presentation to Parliament
options.B: The monthly financial review compares the final grant with the actual expenditure of the year, whereas the Appropriation Accounts compare the monthly actuals with the proportionate budget
options.C: The monthly financial review is an in-year control exercise which compares the actual earnings and expenditure of the period with the proportionate budget for that period, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are prepared after the close of the year and compare the actual expenditure with the Final Grant, explaining the variations
options.D: The monthly financial review is prepared by the Audit Department, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are prepared by the Cash & Pay Office

e: The monthly financial review is an in-year control comparing actual earnings and expenditure with the proportionate budget. The Appropriation Accounts are after the year and compare actual expenditure with the Final Grant, explaining variations.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Final Modification Estimates from a Supplementary Grant?

options.A: The Final Modification Estimates are the last review of the budget, carried out in January, in which the estimates are finally revised with reference to the actuals of the first nine months and the final requirements of the year, whereas a Supplementary Grant is an additional grant voted by Parliament during the year when the amount already granted for a service is found insufficient
options.B: The Final Modification Estimates are voted by Parliament as an additional grant, whereas a Supplementary Grant is an internal review carried out in January
options.C: Both the Final Modification Estimates and a Supplementary Grant are obtained after the close of the financial year
options.D: The Final Modification Estimates can be used to meet expenditure on a new service, whereas a Supplementary Grant cannot be so used

e: Final Modification Estimates are the last January review revising estimates on nine months actuals and final requirements. A Supplementary Grant is an additional grant voted by Parliament during the year when the amount already granted is insufficient.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Extra Budgetary Resources from the internal resources of the Railways?

options.A: Both the resources are generated from the surplus of the Railways and carried in their fund balances
options.B: Extra Budgetary Resources are generated from the revenues of the Railways, whereas the internal resources are borrowed from the market
options.C: Extra Budgetary Resources are voted by Parliament as part of the Demands for Grants, whereas the internal resources require no budgetary provision at all
options.D: Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market, as through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, and their servicing is the responsibility of the Railways, whereas the internal resources are generated by the Railways themselves from their revenues and fund balances and are used to finance a part of the plan outlay

e: Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market, as through IRFC, and serviced by the Railways. Internal resources are generated by the Railways themselves from revenues and fund balances to finance part of the plan outlay.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Consolidated Fund of India from the Contingency Fund of India?

options.A: Both the funds form Part II of the accounts of the Government of India
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India, forming Part I of the Government accounts, receives all the revenues and loans raised by the Government, and no money can be withdrawn from it except under appropriation made by law, whereas the Contingency Fund of India, forming Part II, is an imprest placed at the disposal of the President for meeting urgent unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, the advances from it being recouped after such authorisation
options.C: The Consolidated Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the President for unforeseen expenditure, whereas the Contingency Fund of India receives all the tax revenues of the Government
options.D: Disbursements from both the funds require the prior vote of the Lok Sabha on a Demand for Grant

e: The Consolidated Fund, in Part I, receives all revenues and loans and allows withdrawal only under appropriation by law. The Contingency Fund, in Part II, is an imprest with the President for urgent unforeseen expenditure, recouped after authorisation.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Stores Budget from the Pink Book of the Railways?

options.A: Both the documents list the works approved for inclusion in the Works Programme of the year
options.B: The Stores Budget lists the works approved for the year, whereas the Pink Book estimates the stores requirements of the consuming departments
options.C: The Stores Budget is a derived budget of the stores requirements of the Railways, framed on the basis of the requirements of the consuming departments and the programme of works, whereas the Pink Book is the Works Programme, listing the works approved for inclusion in the year, arranged Plan Head-wise with the provision made for them
options.D: The Stores Budget is voted by Parliament as a separate Demand, whereas the Pink Book is a register maintained in the stores depots

e: The Stores Budget is the derived budget of stores requirements from consuming departments and the works programme. The Pink Book is the Works Programme listing works approved for the year Plan Head-wise with the provision for each.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Classified Abstract from the Debt Head Report of a railway?

options.A: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise summary of the month's transactions, compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted, whereas the Debt Head Report exhibits the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads as recorded in the General Books
options.B: The Classified Abstract exhibits the balances under the debt heads, whereas the Debt Head Report summarises the month's transactions for posting the General Books
options.C: Both the documents are rendered by the stations to the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: The Classified Abstract is prepared by the Audit Department, whereas the Debt Head Report is prepared by the executive departments

e: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise summary of the month transactions from subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted. The Debt Head Report exhibits balances outstanding under debt, suspense and remittance heads.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the books of original entry of a railway from its Ledger?

options.A: Both the books record the transactions finally, head-wise, in the form of accounts
options.B: The books of original entry are the General Books of the railway, whereas the Ledger is a subsidiary book of first record
options.C: The Ledger is maintained only in the executive offices, whereas the books of original entry are maintained only by the Audit Department
options.D: The books of original entry, that is, the subsidiary books such as the Cash Book and the Journal Book, are those in which the transactions are first recorded in detail, whereas the Ledger is the principal book of account in which an account is kept for every head of account and from which the Trial Balance is extracted

e: Books of original entry, like the Cash Book and Journal Book, first record transactions in detail. The Ledger is the principal book keeping an account for every head of account, from which the Trial Balance is extracted.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Contingency Fund of India from the Contingency Fund of a State?

options.A: Both the funds are established by laws made by Parliament under Article 267 of the Constitution
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India is established by a law made by Parliament and is placed at the disposal of the President, whereas the Contingency Fund of a State is established by a law made by the Legislature of the State and is placed at the disposal of the Governor
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the Governor, whereas the Contingency Fund of a State is placed at the disposal of the President
options.D: The Contingency Fund of a State is a part of the Contingency Fund of India, operated through the Reserve Bank of India

e: The Contingency Fund of India is established by a law of Parliament under Article 267 and placed with the President. A State Contingency Fund is established by a law of the State Legislature and placed with the Governor.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Treasury Bills from Cash Management Bills of the Government of India?

options.A: Both the instruments are long-term dated securities issued at a premium
options.B: Treasury Bills are issued to meet temporary mismatches in the cash flow of the Government, whereas Cash Management Bills are issued in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days
options.C: Treasury Bills are zero-coupon instruments, issued at a discount and redeemed at face value, in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days, whereas Cash Management Bills are issued to meet temporary mismatches in the cash flow of the Government and have a maturity of less than 91 days
options.D: Treasury Bills are issued only to the State Governments, whereas Cash Management Bills are issued only to the public sector banks

e: Treasury Bills are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days. Cash Management Bills meet temporary cash flow mismatches and have maturity of less than 91 days.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the tax revenue from the non-tax revenue of the Government of India?

options.A: Tax revenue consists of the compulsory levies imposed by the Government, such as the taxes on income and the goods and services tax, whereas non-tax revenue consists of receipts such as interest on loans, dividends and profits from public sector undertakings, and fees and fines
options.B: Tax revenue consists of the dividends received from public sector undertakings, whereas non-tax revenue consists of the goods and services tax
options.C: Both tax revenue and non-tax revenue are raised only through market borrowings
options.D: Tax revenue is credited to the Public Account of India, whereas non-tax revenue is credited to the Contingency Fund of India

e: Tax revenue consists of compulsory levies like income tax and goods and services tax. Non-tax revenue consists of interest on loans, dividends and profits from public sector undertakings, fees, fines and similar receipts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway from the Financial Commissioner (Railways)?

options.A: Both the officers function as the financial adviser to the General Manager of a zonal railway
options.B: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway is a Member of the Railway Board, whereas the Financial Commissioner heads the accounts organisation of one zonal railway
options.C: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the Financial Commissioner is elected by the Railway Board
options.D: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway, the Principal Financial Adviser, heads the accounts organisation of the railway and functions as the financial adviser to its General Manager, whereas the Financial Commissioner (Railways) is a Member of the Railway Board and its principal financial adviser on matters of railway finance

e: The Principal Financial Adviser heads a zonal railway accounts organisation and advises its General Manager. The Financial Commissioner (Railways) is a Member of the Railway Board and its principal financial adviser on railway finance.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Objectionable Item Register from an inspection report in the railway accounts organisation?

options.A: Both the documents are reports issued by the statutory audit organisation of the Railways
options.B: The Objectionable Item Register is a register maintained in the Accounts Office in which items of expenditure or receipts held under objection during internal check, pending regularisation, are entered and watched till they are cleared, whereas an inspection report is the report by which the findings and objections of the periodical inspection of an accounts office or of the initial records of an executive office, carried out by the Accounts Department, are communicated to the office inspected
options.C: The Objectionable Item Register communicates the findings of an inspection, whereas an inspection report records the items held under objection during internal check
options.D: The Objectionable Item Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas an inspection report is maintained by the Cash & Pay Office

e: The Objectionable Item Register, kept in the Accounts Office, records items held under objection during internal check till regularisation. An inspection report communicates the findings of a periodical inspection of an office by the Accounts Department.
